title: Engineering Ethics Case Report: To Ship or Not to Ship
overview: Individual written report analysing an engineering ethics case inspired by real-world professional scenarios. Students identify and discuss ethical issues, explore stakeholder decision-making, present evidence-based arguments for and against, and conclude with a justified recommended course of action. The selected scenario concerns Rachel, a QA engineer deciding whether to ship potentially defective servers, including a government health department contract.
deliverables: Written report on an engineering ethics case inspired by real-world scenarios faced by engineering professionals.
Identification and discussion of ethical issues associated with the scenario.
Exploration of ethical dilemmas and how stakeholders might make decisions regarding them.
Discussion of issues and considerations both for and against decisions, supported by reputable evidence/sources.
Justified recommended course of action as the report conclusion.

Address the scenario questions: Is this an ethical way to conduct business? How should she determine when to ship a product with known defects? What are the trade-offs in decision making? What should Rachel do?
Reference external case studies to support all arguments.

format.length: Maximum 1,500 words excluding abstract, references and figures; introduction, body and conclusion together must be fewer than 1,500 words; abstract around 150 words.
format.structure: Report must include an abstract (~150 words), introduction, body and conclusion; headings may be used to organise the body; no restrictions on body organisation; figures and tables may be used; references required using a consistent and established style such as Harvard or IEEE.
format.other: Individual submission; references and figures do not count toward the word count; may refer to relevant course lectures/workshops and the Engineers Australia Code of Ethics.

requirements.text: Base the report on the provided Topic 2 scenario: Rachel is a Quality Assurance Engineer at a large electronics company responsible for final testing of servers and part of a team deciding when new products ship; a six-month release cycle limits testing; she will not ship if any possibility of malfunction causing physical harm exists, but will ship a product with higher likelihood of failure causing data loss because a competitor will otherwise.

In the scenario, address that Rachel learns a large contract of servers is being procured by a government health department, where failure can lead directly to improper health administration for hospitals and emergency services and catastrophic business consequences; fulfilling the contract provides significant revenue and growth affecting her employment, and distributing/testing at scale may allow safety design improvements for larger international contracts planned in a few years.
Discuss how stakeholders might make decisions about ethical issues associated with the scenario.
Identify and discuss ethical issues associated with the scenario.
Explore the ethical dilemmas and consider how stakeholders might make decisions regarding them.
Identify and discuss issues and considerations both for and against the decisions.
Use reputable evidence/sources to support arguments.
Conclude the report with a justified recommended course of action.

Do not rely only on stating that an action should be taken because a law or regulation requires it; conclusions must follow thorough research into ethical considerations for all involved stakeholders and a holistic discussion of potential consequences of decisions.
Address whether this is an ethical way to conduct business.
Address how Rachel should determine when to ship a product with known defects and what trade-offs are involved in decision making.
Reference external case studies to support all arguments.
